what_lands_in_tp_3b_i1.design: Single-block, 256 threads, ELEMS_PER_THREAD = n / 256. Phase 1: load x + 4 peer partials, sum-fold into hidden, accumulate sum-of-squares per-thread. Block-reduce sum_sq via __shfl_xor (intra-warp) + LDS (inter-warp). Phase 2: rsqrt(mean_sq + eps), elementwise out_norm[i] = hidden[i] * rsqrt * weight[i].
what_lands_in_tp_3b_i1.wrapper: BarP2pAllReduce::residual_rmsnorm_tp{2,4} (n must be multiple of 256; covers Qwen3.5/3.6 hidden sizes 2048/4096/5120/8192)

what_landed_in_tp_3b_i2.scope: In-layer post-attn fusion only: ar_residual + rmsnorm_f16 → BarP2pAllReduce::residual_rmsnorm_tp{2,4}.
wired_in: world=1 degenerate path retained as add_f16 + rmsnorm_f16 (bit-equivalent reference for parity)
what_landed_in_tp_3b_i2.savings_per_layer_per_token: 1 launch (was 2: AR + rmsnorm; now 1: fused). 64 layers × 1 launch saved = 64 launches/token = ~0.6 ms at 10 µs/launch.

what_remains_in_tp_3b_i3.scope: Cross-layer post-FFN fusion: layer-L FFN-AR + layer-L+1 attn_norm + Q8_1 quantize.
what_remains_in_tp_3b_i3.blocker: Existing forward_full_attn_decode_tp / forward_gdn_decode_tp run rmsnorm_quant_q8_1 (norm + quantize fused) INTERNALLY at the start. To fuse cross-layer, that internal step would need to be lifted to the layer driver and replaced with a fused AR+norm+quantize kernel.
what_remains_in_tp_3b_i3.deferred_reason: Touches the per-layer forward function signature. Safe to defer without affecting V1 ship.

expected_lift_breakdown.lift_source_per_token_ms: ~1.5 ms (eliminates 128 launch round-trips at ~10 µs each)
expected_lift_breakdown.rationale: Each fused launch replaces an AR launch + a norm launch — saves one driver dispatch. 128 launches × 10 µs ≈ 1.3 ms/token. At 60 tok/s budget (16.6 ms), that's ~8% throughput.

bit_exactness.argument: Same arithmetic order: residual sum (FP32 accumulate of same operands), then mean-sq (FP32 sum-of-squares with same reduction tree as flambeau_rmsnorm_f16 — __shfl_xor intra-warp + LDS inter-warp), then rsqrt + elementwise scale. The fused kernel's sum_sq reduction matches the standalone kernel's reduction order modulo the intermediate write to hidden[i]; both produce the same FP32 sum_sq → same rsqrt → same out_norm[i].

notes: Single-block constraint limits n ≤ 256 × 32 (per-thread budget of ~32 floats fits VGPRs cleanly on gfx906). Qwen3.5/3.6 hidden sizes well within bound. For n > 8192 (not in V1 scope), a multi-block kernel with cross-WG atomic barriers (mi50grad's M3 pattern) would be required — TP-4d follow-up if a model needs it.
